name: Burg Laudegg
kurzbeschreibung: Burg Laudegg perches on a vertical slate cliff above Ladis: residential tower from 1200, castle lake, and proud witness to Rhaetian settlement history.
beschreibung:
Overview

The picturesque Burg Laudegg (historically also Laudeck) perches on a steeply falling, vertical slate cliff at 1,176 metres above sea level right beside the idyllic castle lake in the municipality of Ladis. As a prominent landmark of the popular high plateau Serfaus-Fiss-Ladis in the Tyrolean Oberland, the fortification forms an unforgettable photo motif together with the heritage village ensemble and the surrounding peaks of the Samnaungruppe. Its exposed position allowed seamless surveillance of the Upper Inntal and the historic Roman road Via Claudia Augusta from the Early Middle Ages onwards.

History & Architecture

The prominent rocky knoll above the Inntal was already settled during the Bronze and Iron Ages, as confirmed by archaeological finds. The construction of the first stone castle dates back to the early 13th century: around 1200, the Herren von Laudeck built the mighty Romanesque keep. In 1239, the castle was first mentioned in historical records. From 1282, Laudegg served as the sovereign court seat of the Upper Court under Count Meinhard II. von Tirol-Görz. During the dramatic Appenzell Wars in 1406, insurgent peasants burned the castle down; Duke Friedrich IV. with the Empty Pockets had it rebuilt. When Emperor Maximilian I. relocated the court to Schloss Ried in 1500, the complex lost its administrative significance and decayed visibly over the centuries. From 1964 onwards, a dedicated private family acquired the ruins and carried out a masterful, faithful restoration of the walls. The architectural showpiece is the square Romanesque residential tower made of roughly hewn slate blocks, complemented by reconstructed palas quarters, curtain walls, and battlement crowns.

Visit & Arrival

Because Burg Laudegg is privately owned today, the castle interior is only accessible during guided cultural and historical tours in the summer months (usually Wednesdays, advance booking through the tourism board). The outdoor grounds, the promenades around the Lader Burgsee, and the observation balcony are open year-round and freely accessible free of charge. Arrival by public transport: ÖBB express train to Landeck-Zams station, from there take Postbus line 220 up to Ladis (stop Ladis Dorf, then approx. 5 minutes on foot to the lake). By car: Inntalautobahn A12 or S16 to Ried im Oberinntal, then take the state road up to Ladis; parking is available at the village car parks or at the Sonnenbahn Ladis-Fiss valley station.

Tips

The paved circular path around the picturesque castle lake is completely barrier-free and can easily be navigated with strollers and wheelchairs. On the northern shore of the lake, the ancient defensive walls are reflected gorgeously in the crystal-clear water – especially during the evening hours when the castle is atmospherically illuminated. Sample the traditional spring water from the famous Lader Sauerbrunn mineral healing spring on the village square, highly valued for its health benefits since the 16th century.
